'''Vitaliy Khutoryanskiy''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry|FRSC]] [https://apsgb.co.uk/awards/ FAPS] [[FIMMM]] is a British and Kazakhstani scientist,  a Professor of Formulation Science and a Royal Society Industry Fellow at the [[University of Reading]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=University of Reading webpage of Prof Vitaliy Khutoryanskiy |url=https://www.reading.ac.uk/pharmacy/staff/professor-vitaliy-khutoryanskiy }}</ref> His research focuses on polymers, biomaterials, nanomaterials, drug delivery, and pharmaceutical sciences. He also develops alternatives to animal testing, using invertebrates to support the global 3Rs principle of replacing, reducing, and refining animal use in science. Khutoryanskiy has published over 300 original research articles, book chapters, and reviews. His publications have attracted > 17000 citations and his current [[h-index]] is 62.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Scopus preview – Khutoryanskiy, Vitaliy V. – Author details – Scopus |url=https://www.scopus.com/authid/detail.uri?authorId=35606915700 |access-date=2022-09-05 |website=www.scopus.com}}</ref> He received several prestigious awards in recognition for his research in polymers, colloids and drug delivery<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /> as well as for contributions to research peer-review<ref name=":0" /> and mentoring of early career researchers.<ref name=":3" /> He holds several honorary professorship titles from different universities.<ref name=":4" /><ref name=":9">{{Cite web |title=A FAMOUS BRITISH SCIENTIST WAS AWARDED THE TITLE OF HONORARY PROFESSOR OF BUKETOV UNIVERSITY |url=https://buketov.edu.kz/en/media/izvestnomu-britanskomu-uenomu-prisvoeno-zvanie-poetnogo-professora-buketov-university-619}}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Khutoryanskiy was born and grew up in [[Almaty]], Kazakhstan.<ref name=":5" /> He studied at [[Al-Farabi Kazakh National University]], graduating with a BSc in Chemistry in 1996. He earned his MSc in [[Polymer Chemistry]] in 1998, and then his PhD in Polymer Chemistry in 2000, both from the same institution. His PhD project was focused on the studies of hydrogen-bonded interpolymer complexes and preparation of [[hydrophilic]] films.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Z.S. |first1=Nurkeeva |last2=G.A. |first2=Mun |last3=V.V. |first3=Khutoryanskiy |date=2001 |title=Interpolymer complexes of poly(glycol vinyl ethers) and related composite materials |url=https://cyberleninka.ru/article/n/interpolymer-complexes-of-poly-glycol-vinyl-ethers-and-related-composite-materials |journal=Высокомолекулярные соединения. Серия Б |volume=43 |issue=5 |pages=925–935 |issn=2308-1139}}</ref><ref name=":7" /> During his PhD studies, he also spent 4 months in the research group of [[:pl:Janusz Rosiak|Janusz Rosiak]] at [[Łódź University of Technology]], Poland,<ref name=":5" /> where specialised in [[radiation chemistry]] of hydrophilic polymers.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Khutoryanskiy |first1=Vitaliy V. |last2=Kujawa |first2=Piotr |last3=Nurkeeva |first3=Zauresh S. |last4=Rosiak |first4=Janusz M. |date=2001-04-01 |title=Radiation Synthesis of Linear and Crosslinked Poly[2-(methacryloyloxy)ethyl]trimethylammonium Chloride and Complex Formation with Potassium Hexacyanoferrates (II, III) in Aqueous Solutions |url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1002/1521-3935(20010401)202:7<1089::aid-macp1089>3.0.co;2-s |journal=Macromolecular Chemistry and Physics |volume=202 |issue=7 |pages=1089–1093 |doi=10.1002/1521-3935(20010401)202:7<1089::aid-macp1089>3.0.co;2-s |issn=1022-1352|url-access=subscription }}</ref> He worked as a Lecturer in Polymer Science at Al-Farabi Kazakh National University in 2000-2002. In 2002, he moved to the United Kingdom and joined the research group of [[Ijeoma Uchegbu]] at the [[University of Strathclyde]] as a postdoctoral research assistant, where he worked on the synthesis of [[chitosan]] [[amphiphiles]] and their studies for drug delivery.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Qu |first1=Xioazhong |last2=Khutoryanskiy |first2=Vitaliy V. |last3=Stewart |first3=Ailsa |last4=Rahman |first4=Samina |last5=Papahadjopoulos-Sternberg |first5=Brigitte |last6=Dufes |first6=Christine |last7=McCarthy |first7=Dave |last8=Wilson |first8=Clive G. |last9=Lyons |first9=Robert |last10=Carter |first10=Katharine C. |last11=Schätzlein |first11=Andreas |date=2006-12-01 |title=Carbohydrate-Based Micelle Clusters Which Enhance Hydrophobic Drug Bioavailability by Up to 1 Order of Magnitude |url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/bm0604000 |journal=Biomacromolecules |language=en |volume=7 |issue=12 |pages=3452–3459 |doi=10.1021/bm0604000 |pmid=17154474 |issn=1525-7797|url-access=subscription }}</ref> In 2004, he moved to the [[University of Manchester]] to work as a postdoctoral research assistant of Nicola Tirelli, studying the design of oxidation-responsive [[nanoparticle]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Khutoryanskiy |first1=Vitaliy V. |last2=Tirelli |first2=Nicola |date=2008-01-01 |title=Oxidation-responsiveness of nanomaterials for targeting inflammatory reactions |journal=Pure and Applied Chemistry |language=en |volume=80 |issue=8 |pages=1703–1718 |doi=10.1351/pac200880081703 |s2cid=55012679 |issn=1365-3075|doi-access=free }}</ref> In 2005, Khutoryanskiy was appointed as a Lecturer in Pharmaceutics at newly-established Reading School of Pharmacy, [[University of Reading]]. In 2010, he was promoted to Reader (Associate Professor) in Pharmaceutical Materials and in 2014, he became full Professor of Formulation Science.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title="Best PhD supervisor in the UK[1]" discusses pharmaceutics, teaching and karate |url=https://www.reading.ac.uk/pharmacy/stories/vitaliy-khutoryanskiy}}</ref> In 2023, he became the founding director of the Physicochemical, Ex Vivo and Invertebrate Tests and Analysis Centre ([https://pevitac.co.uk/ PEVITAC]) at the University of Reading.

== Research ==
Earlier research of Khutoryanskiy was focused on the studies of hydrogen-bonded [[interpolymer complexes]] formed by poly(carboxylic acids) and various non-ionic polymers in aqueous and organic solvents. He established the factors affecting the complexation between polymers such as solvent nature, pH and ionic strength of solutions, nature and molecular weight of interacting polymers as well as environmental temperature.<ref name=":7">{{Cite journal |title=Effect of copolymer composition on interpolymer complex formation of (co)poly(vinyl ether)s with poly(acrylic acid) in aqueous and == Books ==
He edited and co-edited several books<ref>{{Cite web |title=Amazon.co.uk : Khutoryanskiy |url=https://www.amazon.co.uk/s?k=Khutoryanskiy&crid=3KSDGGP0GLQ5E&sprefix=khutoryanskiy+,aps,123&ref=nb_sb_noss |access-date=2022-09-04 |website=www.amazon.co.uk |language=en-gb}}</ref>

* Hydrogen-bonded Interpolymer Complexes: Formation, Structure and Applications (edited by V.V. Khutoryanskiy and G.Staikos), [[World Scientific]], 2009
* Mucoadhesive Materials and Drug Delivery Systems (edited by V.V. Khutoryanskiy), [[Wiley (publisher)|John Wiley & Sons]], 2014
* Temperature-responsive Polymers: Chemistry, Properties, and Applications (edited by V.V. Khutoryanskiy and T.K. Georgiou), John Wiley & Sons, 2018
* Advances in Mucoadhesive Polymers and Formulations for Transmucosal Drug Delivery (edited by V.V. Khutoryanskiy), MDPI AG, 2020
* Solid Dispersions for Drug Delivery: Applications and Preparation Methods (edited by V.V. Khutoryanskiy and H. Al-Obaidi), MDPI AG, 2022

== Policy and outreach ==
Beyond his research activities, Khutoryanskiy contributes to discussions on science policy and public communication. He has been cited by the UK Science Media Centre for expert views on alternatives to animal testing in cosmetics regulation.<ref>{{Cite web |title=expert reaction to government announcing that no new licences will be issued for animal testing of chemicals used exclusively as cosmetic ingredients {{!}} Science Media Centre |url=https://www.sciencemediacentre.org/expert-reaction-to-government-announcing-that-no-new-licences-will-be-issued-for-animal-testing-of-chemicals-used-exclusively-as-cosmetic-ingredients/ |access-date=2025-11-02 |language=en-GB}}</ref> His letter to ''Chemistry World'' addressing the environmental and health implications of fireworks led to a subsequent debate among readers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=World |first=Chemistry |title=Letters: December 2023 |url=https://www.chemistryworld.com/opinion/letters-december-2023/4018417.article |access-date=2025-11-02 |website=Chemistry World |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=World |first=Chemistry |title=Letters: March 2024 |url=https://www.chemistryworld.com/opinion/letters-march-2024/4019013.article |access-date=2025-11-02 |website=Chemistry World |language=en}}</ref> In 2026, Khutoryanskiy took part in the Royal Society Pairing Scheme, a science-policy programme in which researchers are paired with parliamentarians or civil servants. He was paired with Yuan Yang, MP for Earley and Woodley, and discussed alternatives to animal experimentation, research funding and wider challenges facing UK universities and research.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Byrne |first=Conor |date=2026-04-28 |title=A Week in Westminster - Professor Vitaliy Khutoryanskiy |url=https://research.reading.ac.uk/research-blog/2026/04/28/a-week-in-westminster-professor-vitaliy-khutoryanskiy/ |access-date=2026-05-01 |website=Connecting Research |language=en-GB}}</ref>
